name: Codebase Audit
description: Structured codebase audit: define the criteria and scope, read against them, classify findings by severity, raise work items for the critical ones, and report. Read-only except for the work items it creates.
narrative: An audit measures against a standard; it does not fix. Fix the criteria and the scope first — what "good" means here, and exactly what you are examining — then read through it systematically against them without changing a line. Classify what you find by severity (critical and high first, then the rest), because a flat list hides the findings that matter. Turn the critical and high ones into concrete work items someone can act on, and close with a report: scope, criteria, an honest overall health read, and the ranked findings. Auditing stays read-only; the only things you create are the record and the work items.
